summary: A formula ends in an error value (#DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #REF!, …); #N/A is reported as a warning.
A formula refers to itself, directly or through other cells.
A defined name points nowhere: #REF!, a missing sheet, or a scope sheet that does not exist.
Two merged ranges overlap, which Excel refuses to open cleanly.
A merged range covers cells with values that only its top-left cell shows.
A formula reads a single empty cell beyond its sheet's data, often a typo in a reference.

Cells are set in a font the renderer has no face for, so they are drawn in its built-in face and take other widths than in Excel: add the font, or for an Office font its metric-compatible stand-in (Carlito for Calibri). An Office font drawn in the built-in face while the host has added no fonts at all is the kit's own fallback and is not reported.
A cell's text has characters no face the renderer has draws (such as ✓ or ✗ in Carlito); they show as empty boxes.
A code was found more than 100 times; the rest are counted, not listed.
